sunforge-story.text: Community-first weird western storytelling. Each page should preserve the immediate human stakes before serving the larger mystery. Kael is not staged as a brooding chosen one or secret fugitive; other people assign meaning to him while he remains materially present. Eva's curiosity should come from appetite, risk and affection rather than exposition. Jessa should read social heat and act before discussion becomes procedure. Veyra's control is human investigative pressure, not scientific omniscience. Samuel's manipulation depends on genuine listening and care. Avoid placeholder dialogue rhythms in which one character states the event and another answers with a clipped 'then...' solution. Give each speaker distinct sentence shape, priorities, humor, avoidance and emotional temperature. Sunforges remain observed background facts unless the page itself earns more.
